A.explanation: This inverts the frequency dependence because $n_{max} = d/\lambda$ increases when wavelength decreases, so $f$ must be in the numerator.

B.explanation: With $\sin\theta = 1$ and $\lambda = c/f$, $d = n\lambda$ gives $n = df/c$.

C.explanation: This gives $n = d\lambda$, which has units of $\text{m}^2$ and reverses the $d/\lambda$ ratio from the grating equation.

D.explanation: This is the reciprocal $\lambda/d$, which would decrease when line spacing $d$ increases instead of increase.

walkthrough: Recall the condition for an intensity maximum from a diffraction grating: $d\sin\theta = n\lambda$, where $d$ is the line spacing and $n$ is the order.
The highest order is limited by geometry because $\sin\theta$ cannot exceed $1$. Set $\sin\theta = 1$ for the limiting case, giving $d = n_{max}\lambda$.
The wavelength is not given directly, but monochromatic light of frequency $f$ satisfies $c = f\lambda$, so $\lambda = c/f$.
Rearrange for $n_{max}$: multiply by $f$ and divide by $c$ to get $n_{max} = df/c$. This is option B.
